title: Bharat Semi Raises $24 Mn To Build Smart Sensors For Physical AI
summary: Semiconductor startup Bharat Semi raises 24 million dollars to build physical AI sensors
detailed: Bharat Semi has raised $24 million in a seed funding round to develop programmable smart sensors for physical AI systems.
The round was led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons, and Indus Bridge Ventures, with participation from Micromax and other investors.
Founders Vrinda Kapoor and Vinayak Dalmia lead the Bengaluru-based semiconductor startup, which targets a global AI sensor market projected to reach $139.4 billion by 2033.

This matters because integrating sensing and AI inference onto a single chip reduces component data movement by up to 99% and lowers system costs by up to 10X for edge devices like drones and robotics.
sentences: The round was led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons and Indus Bridge Ventures, with participation from Micromax, Valour Capital, New York-based Gaingels, and angel investors Mukul Agarwal and Kartik Iyer.

The startup plans to deploy the capital towards developing its next generation of products, expanding its engineering teams in India and the US, and accelerating go-to-market efforts with global customers.
Founded in 2021 by Vrinda Kapoor and Vinayak Dalmia, Bharat Semi is developing programmable smart sensors that integrate sensing and AI inference into a single solution.
The technology is designed to enable machines to interpret information and respond to their surroundings in real time, without relying entirely on remote computing infrastructure.
Prior to the advent of AI, conventional sensors primarily captured information and transmitted it to separate processing systems for interpretation.
But edge AI is now creating demand for hardware that can process information closer to where it is captured, reducing latency, power consumption and data movement.
To capture this wave, Bharat Semi is integrating sensing and AI processing, allowing devices to make decisions closer to the point of data capture.

According to the startup, its programmable smart sensors, which can be configured for different applications and AI models, reduce data movement between components by up to 99% and lower system costs by up to 10X compared with conventional multi-chip modules.
Bharat Semi is initially targeting the consumer electronics and surveillance markets, where cost, power consumption and latency are key considerations.
Over the longer term, it plans to extend its technology to robotics, automotive, aerospace and defence applications.
However, the startup is yet to commercialise its technology.

Expected use cases include controlling ceiling fan movement based on visual capture of a sleeping subject, sharing alerts from door cameras when a person or parcel has arrived, or signalling to drones about obstructions in its flight path – all in real time without needing the data to be sent elsewhere.
Bharat Semi is eyeing a share in the global image sensor market, which is expected to reach a size of $49.8 Bn by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 7.7%.

At the same time, the global AI sensor market is expected to grow at a CAGR of 48.8% to reach $139.4 Bn by 2033, according to Grand View Research, highlighting the growing demand for AI-enabled smart sensors.
Bharat Semi will take on established players such as Japan’s Sony Semiconductor Solutions and US-based OmniVision, alongside emerging startups such as Oculi and France-based Prophesee.
